[Section] TF weighted word subspace
[source_id=88] The word subspace formulation presented in Section "Word subspace" is a practical and compact way to represent sets of word vectors, retaining most of the variability of features. However, as seen in the BOW features, the frequency of words is relevant information that can improve the characterization of a text. To incorporate this information into the word subspace modeling, we propose an extension of the word subspace, called the term-frequency (TF) weighted word subspace.
[source_id=89] Like the word subspace, the TF weighted word subspace is mathematically defined as a low-dimensional linear subspace in a word vector space with high dimensionality. However, a weighted version of the PCA BIBREF25 , BIBREF26 is utilized to incorporate the information given by the frequencies of words (term-frequencies). This TF weighted word subspace is equivalent to the word subspace if we consider all occurrences of the words.
[source_id=90] Consider the set of word vectors $\lbrace {x}_c^k\rbrace _{k=1}^{N_c} \in \mathbb {R}^{p}$ , which represents each word in the context $c$ , and the set of weights $\lbrace \omega _i\rbrace _{i=1}^{N_c}$ , which represent the frequencies of the words in the context $c$ .
[source_id=91] We incorporate these frequencies into the subspace calculation by weighting the data matrix ${X}$ as follows:
[source_id=92] $${\widetilde{X}}={X}{\Omega }^{1/2},$$   (Eq. 33)
[source_id=93] where ${X} \in \mathbb {R}^{p \times N_c}$ is a matrix containing the word vectors $\lbrace {x}_c^k\rbrace _{k=1}^{N_c}$ and ${\Omega }$ is a diagonal matrix containing the weights $\lbrace \omega _i\rbrace _{i=1}^{N_c}$ .
[source_id=94] We then perform PCA by solving the SVD of the matrix ${\widetilde{X}}$ :
[source_id=95] $${\widetilde{X}}={AMB}^{\top },$$   (Eq. 34)
[source_id=96] where the columns of the orthogonal matrices ${A}$ and ${B}$ are, respectively, the left-singular vectors and right-singular vectors of the matrix ${\widetilde{X}}$ , and the diagonal matrix ${M}$ contains singular values of ${\widetilde{X}}$ .
[source_id=97] Finally, the orthonormal basis vectors of the $m_c$ -dimensional TF weighted subspace ${W}$ are the column vectors in ${A}$ corresponding to the $m_c$ largest singular values in ${M}$ .
[source_id=98] Text classification with TF weighted word subspace can also be performed under the framework of MSM. In this paper, we will refer to MSM with TF weighted word subspace as TF-MSM.

However, as seen in the BOW features, the frequency of words is relevant information that can improve the characterization of a text. To incorporate this information into the word subspace modeling, we propose an extension of the word subspace, called the term-frequency (TF) weighted word subspace.

Like the word subspace, the TF weighted word subspace is mathematically defined as a low-dimensional linear subspace in a word vector space with high dimensionality. However, a weighted version of the PCA BIBREF25 , BIBREF26 is utilized to incorporate the information given by the frequencies of words (term-frequencies). This TF weighted word subspace is equivalent to the word subspace if we consider all occurrences of the words.
